purpose: Wording rules for the Mae Sai replay. The replay is a historical reconstruction and a planning scenario, so its text must not claim real-time detection, a forecast, an official warning, a validation, return periods or a road schedule, and it must not rank the shelter sets, present a modelled hour as a safe time to leave or tell the reader which shelters to open. One file feeds both linters: apps/web/src/lib/replay-wording-lint.ts (vitest) and src/floodguard/wording_lint.py (pytest).
how_it_works: Text is normalised first: web addresses are removed, runs of white space become one space, curly apostrophes become straight ones, and non-breaking hyphens, figure dashes, en dashes and minus signs become plain hyphens.
Each pattern in allow is then removed, in order. They are explicit negations such as 'not a forecast'. A new negation needs a new entry here; a plain 'not' somewhere in the sentence is not enough.
Whatever still matches a pattern in rules is a finding.

Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions that mean the same in JavaScript (flags iu) and in Python (re.IGNORECASE). Word edges are written as (?<![A-Za-z0-9_]) and (?![A-Za-z0-9_]) because \b treats Thai letters differently in the two engines.

Each Thai rule lists the common renderings of the banned claim, not one spelling: a translator's wording of a banned English claim must fail too. A Thai denial needs its own allow entry, as in English.
thai_terms_review: The Thai terms and denials were widened on 2 Oct 2026 (ตามเวลาจริง, คาดการณ์, ทำนาย, แม่นยำ, ยืนยันแล้ว, ผ่านการตรวจสอบ, ประกาศเตือน, คาบการเกิดซ้ำ, Thai digits), and again the same day for the shelter and road rules (ศูนย์พักพิง, ศูนย์อพยพ, ตารางเวลาปิดถนน, แผนการปิดถนน). The Thai language reviewer has not signed the list off yet (roadmap H12, due 22 Oct 2026).
